title: Western Chalukya Empire
capsule: The Western Chalukyas of Kalyani (also called the Kalyani Chalukyas or Later Chalukyas) were a Deccan dynasty that re-established Chalukya power c.973 when Tailapa II overthrew the Rashtrakuta kingdom, ruling from their capital at Kalyani (modern Basavakalyan, Karnataka). The dynasty reached its apex under Vikramaditya VI (r.1076–1126), who gave his name to the Vikrama Shaka era, commissioned the Vikramankadevacharita from the poet Bilhana, and extended Chalukya influence to the Konkan coast and parts of northern Tamil Nadu through repeated campaigns against the Cholas. The empire disintegrated after 1126 as the feudatory Hoysala, Kalachuri, and Yadava chiefs asserted independence; the last Kalyani Chalukya king was overthrown by the Kalachuris c.1189.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Western Chalukya core territory in the Deccan is attested by copper-plate grants and stone inscriptions; the outer extent of suzerainty, especially in coastal and Tamil regions, is inferred from military campaign records and is spatially approximate.
